_about: Step-slice cases (slice.py): one work item, run from step-plan to the end of its inner loop on a fixture repository. The prompt is the step's request; work_item is what the seed records as the plan's only item; checks run in a clean export of the product worktree's HEAD; expect_paths are fnmatch patterns the item's commits must touch. A case with a seeded_defect plants a latent defect its own checks do not exercise: probe commands (run by seeded_defects.py on the final tree, never part of the verdicts) fail when the defect survived, and tree names the reference trees under fixtures/ (naive: what a run with no review leaves; fixed: the corrected tree) that prove the probe tells them apart.

node-add-function.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a function slugify(text) to src/strings.js and export it. It lower-cases the text, turns every run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 into one hyphen, and trims hyphens from both ends: slugify('  Hello, World! ') returns 'hello-world' and slugify('') returns ''. A non-string argument throws a TypeError, like the other helpers. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Add slugify(text) to src/strings.js
work_item.context: Lower-case; each run of non [a-z0-9] characters becomes one hyphen; trim hyphens at both ends; TypeError for a non-string; node:test tests.

node-fix-bug.prompt: In this Node.js project, paginate() in src/paginate.js loses the last page whenever the number of items is not a multiple of the page size: paginate([1,2,3,4,5], 3, 2) returns no items and reports 2 pages, but it should return { page: 3, pages: 3, items: [5] }. Fix the bug and add a regression test; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Fix paginate() dropping the last partial page
work_item.context: paginate([1,2,3,4,5], 3, 2) must return { page: 3, pages: 3, items: [5] }; add a regression test.

node-add-route.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a health route to the HTTP server in src/server.js: GET /health answers 200 with the JSON body {"ok":true} and a content-type of application/json. The existing routes must keep working. Cover it with a node:test test; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Add GET /health to src/server.js
work_item.context: GET /health -> 200, application/json, body {"ok":true}; existing routes unchanged; node:test test.

node-rename.prompt: In this Node.js project, rename getUser to findUser everywhere: its definition and export in src/users.js, its use in src/server.js, and the tests. Behaviour must not change and no getUser alias may remain. npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Rename getUser to findUser across the project
work_item.context: Definition, export, server use and tests; no behaviour change; no getUser left anywhere.

node-seeded-case-compare.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a function sortNames(names) in a new module src/names.js and export it. It returns a new array with the names in ascending code-point order, which is case-sensitive: every upper-case letter sorts before every lower-case one, so sortNames(['bob', 'Zed', 'alice']) returns ['Zed', 'alice', 'bob']. The argument is not changed, and a non-array argument throws a TypeError. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Add sortNames(names) to src/names.js
work_item.context: Ascending code-point order, case-sensitive (upper-case before lower-case); new array; TypeError for a non-array; node:test tests.

seeded_defect.what: an ordering that ignores letter case where the request says it must not (a locale-aware comparator)

node-seeded-numeric-sort.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a function topScores(scores, n) in a new module src/scores.js and export it. It returns the n largest numbers of scores, largest first, as a new array; an n larger than the length returns all of them, and scores is not changed. A non-array scores throws a TypeError. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Add topScores(scores, n) to src/scores.js
work_item.context: The n largest numbers, largest first; new array; n above the length returns all; TypeError for a non-array; node:test tests.

seeded_defect.what: a comparator-less sort, which orders numbers as text ('100' before '9')

node-seeded-empty-guard.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a function mean(values) in a new module src/mean.js and export it. It returns the arithmetic mean of an array of numbers; the mean of an empty array is 0, not NaN. A non-array argument throws a TypeError. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Add mean(values) to src/mean.js
work_item.context: Arithmetic mean; an empty array gives 0, not NaN; TypeError for a non-array; node:test tests.

seeded_defect.what: a division by the length with no guard for an empty input (NaN where the request names 0)
